checks.name: central_question_resolved
checks.evidence: ch 31: Ila neither maps the passes for the queen alone nor hides them for Neshar. She draws two identical true maps under Neshar's names, co-signed 'Ila, surveyor' and 'Kunal of Neshar', and sets them before Sarala and Old Bhim 'at the same moment'. The queen keeps the map and grants the petition. Only series matters stay open in ch 32: Pritam's escape east, the two readings of 'carried till no thaw', the sealed Under-Cairn until the fourth winter, Kiran's reaction and the grey-bearded officer.

checks.name: clues_paid_off
checks.evidence: Every non-series clue pays off on the page. C01 ch 32 (Pritam escapes by a stair inside the north wall; Ila: 'Two spans.'). C02 ch 16 (letter opened at the Glass Lakes). C03 ch 31 (the map carries Neshar's route-names: Old Woman's Tooth, Where the Drum Answers, Widow's Knuckle). C04 ch 28 ('They took the whistle off him after'). C05 ch 26 ('Eleven paces left of the boom line'; the pursuing pair goes through). C06 ch 16 (the letter names Harish as Udai's guest). C07 ch 29 (a shelf of folded gloves, with Harish's place empty). C09 ch 32 (the Hemkot and Neshar readings of 'carried' set against each other). C10 ch 30 and ch 32 (Pasang: 'The way was for the regent Pritam'; Raghu's men's bells found beside Pritam's tracks). C11 ch 31 (day 35: the rope goes quiet and Kunal walks sixteen spans). C12 ch 31 (pace re-measured at one and three-quarter spans; new spans-and-ropes scale bar). C13 ch 24 and ch 28 ('There was no walnut because there was no Dhanu'). C14 ch 31 and ch 32 (the east bearing is logged as seen but not walked, then becomes Pritam's dotted 'unknown way'; payoff moved from the outlined ch 29). C17 ch 30 (the whitening repeats in front of Pasang, who names it). C20 ch 28 (Ila tells the whole letter early). C21 ch 31 (identical copies handed over at the same hour). C08, C15, C16, C18 and C19 are series threads. No clue does neither.

checks.name: midpoint_reversal
checks.evidence: ch 16, the midpoint chapter in a 32-chapter book: the letter reveals that Prince Udai guided Warden Harish, Ila's grandfather, to the Under-Cairn and Harish did not come home. 'It was not neat. It was a receipt.' This recasts the folded gloves (ch 11) and the family rule (ch 10). It changes the romance: the first kiss happens in the same chapter, and then her chosen silence becomes 'a wall he can see but not name' (ch 17), which drives chs 17 to 28.

checks.name: heroine_belief_change
checks.evidence: ch 31: Ila breaks her crown-exclusivity oath in front of the queen. She co-signs the Shared Map under Neshar's names and hands identical copies to Sarala and Bhim, saying: 'I made a promise to him in the salt house, and no mountain made me keep it. After the thirty-fifth day nothing did. I'd rather break the oath I swore than the one I chose.' She then refuses the queen a private first reading of the rubbing: 'Not alone, Majesty. Kunal reads it with you, or neither of you does.' In ch 1 she believed 'A map was true or it was false' and that a true line 'serves whoever reads it' (ch 2). She could not have signed a map as belonging to anyone, or given up the Chief Surveyor's chair for it.

checks.name: real_loss
checks.evidence: ch 26 and ch 28: Dhanu dies under interrogation in the Drum's open water. Gauri lays stones over him at the fold (ch 28), he is not restored, and the crag 'Dhanu's Rest' is named for him in ch 31. Further permanent losses: Ila's two smallest left toes (ch 26), Kunal's right fingertips (ch 21), and Ila's Chief Surveyor commission and place on the crown roll (ch 31).

checks.name: love_interest_goal
checks.evidence: chs 2, 8, 22 and 31: Kunal's own goal is the hill council's petition for self-rule, 'No garrisons in the hill villages... And a seat for Neshar's council at Taravan, won at the thaw' (ch 8). He drafts it during the storm (ch 17), rehearses it with Dhanu (ch 22), and presents it in ch 31, where he stakes his own person as surety against Pritam's escape.

checks.name: series_hinge
checks.evidence: ch 32: a rider reports that Pritam has escaped by the hidden stair in the north wall. The lower door was opened with a key, and no one knows whose. His tracks run east up an undrawn line of cairn-light. Ila draws the dotted line 'unknown way. Pritam.' The queen sets a deadline ('until the snow closes the pass') with Kunal's seat at stake. 'Carried till no thaw' stays open between two readings, the Under-Cairn is sealed until the fourth winter, and Bindu says 'The door will not stay shut.' The teaser has Lata asking about the grey-bearded officer.

series_threads.thread: The Under-Cairn door's three nested loops match the Asha's-crew bundle in Meera's sketch ('Same as cairn'). The link is noted in ch 29 and left unanswered.
Paid off as Pritam's escape route (ch 32), but where the east way leads and who is waiting there stay open for book 2. Payoff moved from the outlined ch 29 to chs 31 and 32.

Kiran asked to hear first where the Bargain is paid. In ch 32 he stares at the rubbing, goes white at the ear rim and touches the 'thaw' sign without speaking. The queen glances at him when sealing the Under-Cairn.
The red thread of the queen's blood in the archive and pardon wax (chs 3 and 30) is not explained.
Nimmi will not name the grey-bearded officer who stood the torches down. Meera keeps a blank ruled line for him in the count, and Lata asks about him in the teaser (ch 32).
The carving's narrow hand measures as a woman's (Hemi), which contradicts 'two brothers in arms' (ch 29). Its meaning for the Bargain is not followed up.

summary: The Winter Oath meets every book-level promise in canon/novel-structure.md. The central question is answered in ch 31: Ila maps the passes for both the queen and Neshar, and that choice proves her changed belief. Her stated words show the change: she would rather break the oath she swore than the one she chose. She also refuses the queen a private first reading. The ch 16 midpoint letter recasts the folded gloves and the princes' way rule, and it reshapes the romance through her chosen silence. Dhanu's death is a real loss that stays lost, along with Ila's toes, Kunal's fingertips and her Chief Surveyor commission. Kunal pursues his own petition (no garrisons, a Taravan seat) throughout. All 16 non-series clues pay off; C14's payoff moves from ch 29 to chs 31 and 32. Five clues (C08, C15, C16, C18, C19) are logged as series threads, and C14's continuation is also logged. Ch 32 delivers a strong hinge: Pritam escapes through the void Ila measured in ch 1 using an unknown key, the meaning of 'carried till no thaw' stays open, and there is a teaser. Points for the owner: the timeline differs from the outline but is internally consistent (outline ch 17 'day twenty' is day ten on the page; outline ch 30 'day thirty-two' is day sixteen; the copying runs about forty days instead of twelve). Raghu's family-crossing motive (ch 30) is left ambiguous and could be developed in book 2.
